10.5],[-63.9,10.5]]];
```{ojs}
  const SETTING = {S: "a subduction zone (one plate dives under another)", R: "a rift zone (plates pull apart)", I: "the middle of a plate (a hot spot)", U: "an unknown setting"};
  const REGIONS = [
    {key: "world", label: "Whole world"},
    {key: "med", label: "Mediterranean", box: [-6, 30, 36, 46]},
    {key: "rift", label: "Great Rift Valley", box: [28, -16, 43, 16]},
    {key: "japan", label: "Japan", box: [128, 30, 146, 46]},
    {key: "sea", label: "SE Asia", box: [92, 5, 110, 28]},
    {key: "andes", label: "Andes", box: [-81, -56, -64, 11]}
  ];
  const W = 960;
  const reduceMotion = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
  const now = Date.now();
  const thisYear = new Date().getFullYear();

  // Data -------------------------------------------------------------
  const volcanoes = VOLC.map(([lon, lat, name, last, country, set, type]) => ({lon, lat, name, last, country, set, type}));
  const recentVolc = v => v.last != null && v.last >= 1900;
  const quakes = u3hQuakes || [];

  // Points every ~0.5° along the plate boundaries, binned on a 2° grid,
  // so we can measure how far each quake is from the nearest boundary.
  const bins = new Map();
  const binKey = (lon, lat) => `${Math.floor(lon / 2)},${Math.floor(lat / 2)}`;
  for (const line of PLATES) {
    for (let i = 1; i < line.length; i++) {
      const a = line[i - 1], b = line[i];
      if (Math.abs(a[0] - b[0]) > 180) continue;
      const interp = d3.geoInterpolate(a, b);
      const n = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(d3.geoDistance(a, b) / (0.5 * Math.PI / 180)));
      for (let k = 0; k <= n; k++) {
        const p = interp(k / n), key = binKey(p[0], p[1]);
        if (!bins.has(key)) bins.set(key, []);
        bins.get(key).push(p);
      }
    }
  }
  const KM = 6371;
  const nearBoundaryKm = (lon, lat, limitKm) => {
    const r = Math.ceil(limitKm / 222) + 1;
    const bx = Math.floor(lon / 2), by = Math.floor(lat / 2);
    let best = Infinity;
    for (let dx = -r; dx <= r; dx++) for (let dy = -r; dy <= r; dy++) {
      let x = bx + dx; if (x < -90) x += 180; if (x >= 90) x -= 180;
      const pts = bins.get(`${x},${by + dy}`);
      if (!pts) continue;
      for (const p of pts) { const d = d3.geoDistance([lon, lat], p) * KM; if (d < best) best = d; }
    }
    return best;
  };
  for (const q of quakes) q.nearKm = nearBoundaryKm(q.lon, q.lat, 300);

  // Map ---------------------------------------------------------------
  // Centered on the Pacific so the "Ring of Fire" shows as one loop
  const projection = d3.geoEqualEarth().rotate([-150, 0]).fitWidth(W, {type: "Sphere"});
  const pathGen = d3.geoPath(projection);
  const [[, y0], [, y1]] = pathGen.bounds({type: "Sphere"});
  const H = Math.ceil(y1 - y0) + 2;

  const svg = d3.create("svg")
    .attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`)
    .attr("role", "img")
    .attr("aria-label", `World map centered on the Pacific Ocean. Orange lines show tectonic plate boundaries. Red triangles show ${volcanoes.length.toLocaleString()} volcanoes active in the last 12,000 years, and yellow dots show ${quakes.length ? quakes.length + " magnitude 4.5 and larger earthquakes from the past 30 days" : "recent earthquakes when live data is available"}. Most volcanoes and earthquakes line up along the plate boundaries, especially the ring around the Pacific Ocean.`);

  const defs = svg.append("defs");
  const glow = defs.append("filter").attr("id", "u3h-glow").attr("x", "-20%").attr("y", "-20%").attr("width", "140%").attr("height", "140%");
  glow.append("feGaussianBlur").attr("stdDeviation", 2.2).attr("result", "b");
  const merge = glow.append("feMerge"); merge.append("feMergeNode").attr("in", "b"); merge.append("feMergeNode").attr("in", "SourceGraphic");

  svg.append("path").attr("d", pathGen({type: "Sphere"})).attr("fill", "#0f1d33");
  svg.append("path").attr("d", pathGen(d3.geoGraticule10())).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "rgba(148,163,184,0.12)").attr("stroke-width", 0.6);
  if (u3hLand) svg.append("path").attr("d", pathGen(u3hLand)).attr("fill", "#3a3530").attr("stroke", "rgba(231,229,228,0.25)").attr("stroke-width", 0.5);

  const gRegion = svg.append("g");
  const gPlates = svg.append("g").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#fb923c").attr("stroke-width", 1.6).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round").attr("filter", "url(#u3h-glow)");
  const platePaths = gPlates.selectAll("path")
    .data(PLATES.map(c => ({type: "LineString", coordinates: c})))
    .join("path").attr("d", pathGen);

  const tri = d3.symbol(d3.symbolTriangle);
  const gVolc = svg.append("g");
  gVolc.selectAll("path").data(volcanoes).join("path")
    .attr("transform", d => { const p = projection([d.lon, d.lat]); return `translate(${p[0]},${p[1]})`; })
    .attr("d", d => tri.size(recentVolc(d) ? 48 : 22)())
    .attr("fill", d => recentVolc(d) ? "#ef4444" : "#b45309")
    .attr("fill-opacity", d => recentVolc(d) ? 0.95 : 0.6)
    .attr("stroke", "#1c1917").attr("stroke-width", 0.5);

  const qr = m => 1.4 * Math.pow(1.6, m - 4.5) + 1.6;
  const gQuake = svg.append("g");
  gQuake.selectAll("circle").data(quakes).join("circle")
    .attr("cx", d => projection([d.lon, d.lat])[0])
    .attr("cy", d => projection([d.lon, d.lat])[1])
    .attr("r", d => qr(d.mag))
    .attr("fill", "#facc15").attr("fill-opacity", 0.7)
    .attr("stroke", "#1c1917").attr("stroke-width", 0.5);

  const selRing = svg.append("circle").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-width", 2).style("display", "none");

  // Layer toggles -------------------------------------------------------
  const layers = {plates: true, volc: true, quake: !!quakes.length};
  const chip = (label, sw, key) => {
    const b = html`<button type="button" class="u3h-chip" aria-pressed="${layers[key]}"><span class="u3h-sw ${sw}" aria-hidden="true"></span>${label}</button>`;
    if (key === "quake" && !quakes.length) b.disabled = true;
    b.onclick = () => { layers[key] = !layers[key]; b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", layers[key]); applyLayers(); };
    return b;
  };
  const applyLayers = () => {
    gPlates.style("display", layers.plates ? null : "none");
    gVolc.style("display", layers.volc ? null : "none");
    gQuake.style("display", layers.quake ? null : "none");
  };

  // Region boxes (the five regions in the unit performance task) ------------
  const boxGeo = ([x0, s, x1, n]) => {
    const ring = [];
    for (let x = x0; x <= x1; x += 1) ring.push([x, s]);
    for (let y = s; y <= n; y += 1) ring.push([x1, y]);
    for (let x = x1; x >= x0; x -= 1) ring.push([x, n]);
    for (let y = n; y >= s; y -= 1) ring.push([x0, y]);
    return {type: "LineString", coordinates: ring};
  };
  const inBox = (d, [x0, s, x1, n]) => d.lon >= x0 && d.lon <= x1 && d.lat >= s && d.lat <= n;
  const regionBtns = REGIONS.map(r => {
    const b = html`<button type="button" class="u3h-chip" aria-pressed="${r.key === "world"}">${r.label}</button>`;
    b.onclick = () => selectRegion(r);
    r.btn = b;
    return b;
  });

  // Readouts ------------------------------------------------------------
  const readout = html`<p class="u3h-readout" aria-live="polite"></p>`;
  const nVolc = volcanoes.length;
  const nPlateVolc = volcanoes.filter(v => v.set === "S" || v.set === "R").length;
  const nQuakeNear = quakes.filter(q => q.nearKm <= 300).length;
  const worldText = () => quakes.length
    ? `Tap any triangle or dot to read about it. <b>${nQuakeNear} of ${quakes.length}</b> big earthquakes in the past 30 days struck within 300 km of a plate boundary.`
    : `Tap any triangle to read about that volcano. (Live earthquake data couldn't load right now, so the quake layer is off.)`;
  readout.innerHTML = worldText();

  const selectRegion = r => {
    REGIONS.forEach(o => o.btn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", o === r));
    gRegion.selectAll("*").remove();
    selRing.style("display", "none");
    if (!r.box) { readout.innerHTML = worldText(); return; }
    gRegion.append("path").attr("d", pathGen(boxGeo(r.box)))
      .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-width", 2).attr("stroke-dasharray", "6 4");
    const v = volcanoes.filter(d => inBox(d, r.box));
    const vr = v.filter(recentVolc).length;
    const q = quakes.filter(d => inBox(d, r.box)).length;
    readout.innerHTML = `<b>${r.label}</b> (dashed box): ${v.length} volcanoes active in the last 12,000 years, ${vr} of them erupting since 1900` +
      (quakes.length ? `, and ${q} big earthquake${q === 1 ? "" : "s"} in the past 30 days.` : ".") +
      ` This is one of the five regions in your performance task.`;
  };

  // Tap to identify ---------------------------------------------------------
  const ago = t => { const d = Math.floor((now - t) / 864e5); return d < 1 ? "today" : `${d} day${d === 1 ? "" : "s"} ago`; };
  const svgNode = svg.node();
  svgNode.addEventListener("click", e => {
    const b = svgNode.getBoundingClientRect();
    const px = (e.clientX - b.left) * W / b.width, py = (e.clientY - b.top) * H / b.height;
    const tol = 16 * W / b.width;
    let best = null, bestD = tol;
    const consider = (d, kind) => {
      const p = projection([d.lon, d.lat]);
      const dist = Math.hypot(p[0] - px, p[1] - py);
      if (dist < bestD) { bestD = dist; best = {d, kind, p}; }
    };
    if (layers.quake) quakes.forEach(d => consider(d, "quake"));
    if (layers.volc) volcanoes.forEach(d => consider(d, "volc"));
    if (!best) { selRing.style("display", "none"); return; }
    selRing.attr("cx", best.p[0]).attr("cy", best.p[1]).attr("r", 9).style("display", null);
    const d = best.d;
    if (best.kind === "volc") {
      const when = d.last == null ? "no known date for its last eruption"
        : d.last >= thisYear - 1 ? `erupting as recently as ${d.last}`
        : d.last < 0 ? `last erupted around ${(-d.last).toLocaleString()} BCE` : `last erupted in ${d.last}`;
      readout.innerHTML = `🌋 <b>${d.name}</b> (${d.country}) · ${d.type.toLowerCase() || "volcano"} · sits at ${SETTING[d.set]} · ${when}.`;
    } else {
      const near = d.nearKm <= 300 ? `about ${Math.round(d.nearKm / 10) * 10} km from a plate boundary` : `more than 300 km from a plate boundary`;
      readout.innerHTML = `💥 <b>M${d.mag.toFixed(1)}</b> · ${d.place} · ${ago(d.time)} · ${Math.round(d.depth)} km deep · ${near}.`;
    }
  });

  // Draw-in animation, only once the map scrolls into view --------------------
  if (!reduceMotion) {
    platePaths.each(function () { const L = this.getTotalLength(); d3.select(this).attr("stroke-dasharray", `${L} ${L}`).attr("stroke-dashoffset", L); });
    gVolc.attr("opacity", 0); gQuake.attr("opacity", 0);
    const io = new IntersectionObserver(([e]) => {
      if (!e.isIntersecting) return;
      io.disconnect();
      platePaths.transition().duration(1800).ease(d3.easeCubicInOut).attr("stroke-dashoffset", 0)
        .on("end", function () { d3.select(this).attr("stroke-dasharray", null); });
      gVolc.transition().delay(1200).duration(700).attr("opacity", 1);
      gQuake.transition().delay(1700).duration(700).attr("opacity", 1);
    }, {threshold: 0.25});
    io.observe(svgNode);
    invalidation.then(() => { io.disconnect(); svg.selectAll("*").interrupt(); });
  }
  applyLayers();

  const stats = html`<div class="u3h-stats">
    <div class="u3h-stat"><strong>${Math.round(100 * nPlateVolc / nVolc)}%</strong>of Earth's ${nVolc.toLocaleString()} recently active volcanoes sit where plates <b>dive under</b> or <b>pull apart</b> from each other.</div>
    ${quakes.length ? html`<div class="u3h-stat"><strong>${Math.round(100 * nQuakeNear / quakes.length)}%</strong>of the past 30 days' big earthquakes (M4.5+) struck within 300 km of a plate boundary.</div>` : ""}
  </div>`;

  return html`<div class="u3h-map-card">
    <div class="u3h-controls" role="group" aria-label="Map layers">
      <p class="u3h-controls-label">Show on the map</p>
      ${chip("Plate boundaries", "u3h-sw-line", "plates")}
      ${chip("Volcanoes", "u3h-sw-tri", "volc")}
      ${chip("Earthquakes (30 days)", "u3h-sw-dot", "quake")}
    </div>
    <div class="u3h-map">${svgNode}</div>
    ${readout}
    <div class="u3h-controls" role="group" aria-label="Zoom in on a region">
      <p class="u3h-controls-label">Check a performance-task region</p>
      ${regionBtns}
    </div>
    ${stats}
  </div>`;
}
```

Volcanoes: <a href="https://volcano.si.edu/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program</a>, Holocene volcano list (active in the last ~12,000 years), downloaded Nov 2026. // If it can't load, the earthquake layer is turned off (no made-up dots).
```{ojs}
u3hQuakes = d3.json("https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/summary/4.5_month.geojson")
  .then(feed => feed.features
    .filter(f => f.geometry && f.properties.mag != null)
    .map(f => ({
      lon: f.geometry.coordinates[0],
      lat: f.geometry.coordinates[1],
      depth: f.geometry.coordinates[2],
      mag: f.properties.mag,
      place: f.properties.place || "Unknown location",
      time: f.properties.time
    }))
    .sort((a, b) => a.mag - b.mag))
  .catch(() => null)
```

## Anchor Phenomenon

> **Major earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and tsunamis happen all over the world, causing loss of life and property, yet humans have been living continuously in these hazardous areas for thousands of years.**
>
> In 2011, an earthquake and tsunami in Japan caused a nuclear disaster that we are still recovering from. In 2022, a volcanic eruption at Tonga was heard thousands of miles away and produced a massive tsunami. Natural disasters caused by tectonic plate movement, like these, are not new to Earth's history, and have long played a part in human societies.

## Unit Driving Question

> **What locations on Earth are most at risk of loss of life and property caused by an earthquake, volcanic eruption, or tsunami in the near future? Why do populations live in these risky areas?**

**Performance task:** The United Nations, non-profits, and governments have limited money to reduce disaster risk. Investigate seismic disasters to **model how they occur**, **explain how they have affected populations** in five at-risk regions (the Mediterranean Basin, the Great Rift Valley, the Japanese Archipelago, Mainland Southeast Asia, and the Andes), and explain how technology and preparedness can guide where resources go.

## Unit Storyline

| Lesson | Question |
|---|---|
| [Unit Opening](unit3-opening.qmd) | Who's at risk from earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and tsunamis, and why do people live there? |
| [Earth's Interior](unit3-earth-interior.qmd) | Where did the material for new islands come from after Krakatoa erupted? |
| [Surface Features & Plate Boundaries](unit3-plate-boundaries.qmd) | Why does seismic activity happen in some areas more than others? |
| [Energy and Matter](unit3-energy-matter.qmd) | Where is all the energy coming from to move plates apart? What processes inside Earth can cause it to reach the surface? And why do people continue to live in these hazardous areas? |
| [Unit Closing](unit3-closing.qmd) | What locations on Earth are most at risk of loss of life and property in the near future? |

## What You'll Figure Out

By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

::: {.key-idea}
- 🌐 **Explain** how seismic waves reveal Earth's layers, and how density sorted those layers
- 🏝️ **Model** how the rock cycle brings material from Earth's interior to the surface to build new islands
- 🧭 **Use** patterns in seismic activity and ocean-floor age as evidence for plate tectonics
- 🌋 **Explain** why the strongest earthquakes, eruptions, and tsunamis happen at convergent plate boundaries
- 🔥 **Model** how radioactive decay and mantle convection move energy and matter to drive plate motion
- ⛏️ **Explain** why tectonically active regions are also rich in resources, and why people live there
- 🛡️ **Explain** how technology and preparedness reduce the impact of hazards, and use that to decide where resources should go
:::
